title: CMS: Online Provider Directory Review Report (Medicare Advantage, round 3, 2017-2018)

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date; findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: U.S. Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
reliability: Government regulator; it reviewed health plans (not practices) and took compliance actions, so it has an interest in showing directory problems. Publication date inferred from the file name.
findings: CMS reviewed 108 providers for each of 52 Medicare Advantage organizations (5,602 providers at 10,504 locations) between November 2017 and July 2018 by calling provider offices.

CMS found 48.74% of listed provider locations had at least one inaccuracy (provider not at location, wrong phone number, or not accepting new patients when listed as accepting); per-plan rates ranged from 4.63% to 93.02%.
Table 1 of the report gives 45.10% deficient locations in round 1 (54 MAOs) and 55.07% in round 2 (64 MAOs); CMS says the rounds are not directly comparable because of minor methodology updates.
The review covered cardiologists, oncologists, ophthalmologists and primary care physicians only.
limitations: Data are from 2016-2018 and cover Medicare Advantage only; later rounds or changes were not read.
Report measures directory accuracy, not the time practices spend; it does not attribute errors to practice-side update burden versus plan-side processing.
Report was fetched from cms.gov but the exact publication date is inferred from the file name.
